Dear Students: As part of my interview process and during my time here, I have learned that members of the community are interested in developing a center that addresses the needs of women and individuals along the gender spectrum. I am appreciative of those who engaged in this work and believe these efforts have positioned us to become a better, more inclusive school today. I am committed to leading a College that empowers all of our students to lead meaningfully better lives and to enjoy successful professional careers. In 2012, a group of faculty, staff and students, came forward with a formal recommendation to establish a women’s center. They framed their recommendation in the context of meeting our 2020 goals. In our endeavors to increase academic excellence, strong female students must be attracted to and retained at the College. A women’s center will serve to support women leaders across campus and enhance our learning-focused community. Establishing a women’s center will aim to increase and stabilize enrollment and revenue as required in the school financial model. Additionally, it will generate a level of engagement and enthusiasm for students, faculty, and staff, serving as a safe space for meaningful dialogue and engaging interactions. Recognizing that diversity is both a reflection of our world and a source of rich education, the College women’s center will make visible a commitment to gender diversity and experience on campus. I acknowledge, as did those who crafted the 2012 proposal, that the establishment of a women’s center will not, in and of itself, fully address our women’s enrollment or climate challenges. I also understand that members of our community desire services that reflect our recognition that gender is a constructed identity and biology and identity are not the same. It is my hope that the establishment of a women’s center will serve as the next positive step in our journey to be a more inclusive community.
I have asked our Chief Diversity Officer, to develop and launch a women’s center. She, with support from our Assistant Director for the Center for Service and Civic Engagement, will build on the work from 2012, as well as more recent proposals, and immediately begin to lead a campus-wide effort to determine the center’s mission, location, name, short and long term goals, and staffing needs.
For this center to achieve its full potential, it is essential that we gather a wide range of perspectives, particularly from students. You will soon receive information regarding opportunities to share your input and help create a center that meets your needs. I encourage your participation in this important process.
